/-!
# Conjecture 5.55

by J. Wiegold

Find a finite $p$-group that cannot be embedded in a finite $p$-group with trivial
multiplicator. Notice that every finite group can be embedded in a group with trivial
multiplicator.

The multiplicator (Schur multiplier) of a group $H$ is the second integral homology group
$M(H) = H_2(H, \mathbb{Z})$; for finite $H$ it is isomorphic to $H^2(H, \mathbb{C}^\times)$.
It is expressed here as `groupHomology.H2 (Rep.trivial ℤ H ℤ)`, the second homology of $H$
with coefficients in $\mathbb{Z}$ regarded as a trivial $H$-module. "Trivial multiplicator"
means that this group is a subsingleton.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem subsingleton_H2_of_subsingleton (H : Type) [Group H] [Subsingleton H] :
    Subsingleton (groupHomology.H2 (Rep.trivial ℤ H ℤ)) :=
  ModuleCat.subsingleton_of_isZero <|
    isZero_groupHomology_succ_of_subsingleton (Rep.trivial ℤ H ℤ) 1

blocks.docstring:
Find a finite $p$-group that cannot be embedded in a finite $p$-group with trivial
multiplicator.

That is, do there exist a prime $p$ and a finite $p$-group $G$ such that no finite $p$-group
$H$ (for the same prime $p$) with trivial Schur multiplier $H_2(H, \mathbb{Z})$ contains a
subgroup isomorphic to $G$, i.e. such that there is no injective group homomorphism
$G \to H$ for any such $H$?

blocks.docstring:
Every finite group can be embedded in a group with trivial multiplicator.

The notebook does not say that the ambient group is finite, but the known result is that every
finite group $G$ embeds in a *finite* group $H$ with trivial Schur multiplier
$H_2(H, \mathbb{Z})$; this is the version stated here. The version with an arbitrary ambient
group is a consequence of it.

claims.decomposer_note: An existence question (open, so answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ ...): does there exist a prime p and a finite p-group G such that for every finite p-group H (same prime p) with trivial Schur multiplier (multiplicator = H_2(H,ℤ) ≅ H^2(H,ℂ^×), expressible via Mathlib's groupHomology) there is no injective group homomorphism G → H; 'Find' presupposes existence but no candidate p-group is given, and the prime p is implicitly existentially quantified.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same mathematics: answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ prime p and finite p-group G (IsPGroup p G, Finite G) such that for every finite p-group H for the same p with Subsingleton H₂(H,ℤ) (groupHomology of Rep.trivial ℤ H ℤ in degree 2) there is no injective hom G →* H. c01's declaration was used with minor edits: `groupHomology.H2` (Mathlib abbrev for degree-2 homology) for readability and `¬ ∃ f, Injective f` as in c02/c05–c08. Names match the slot exactly (c04/c06 give the variant a different full name). Checked: p.Prime is required (IsPGroup degenerate for p=0,1); the ∀ H hypothesis is non-vacuous (test theorem shows trivial group has trivial multiplier; cyclic p-groups too); universe Type is harmless for finite groups; answer(True) ↔ such a G exists.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 5.55

by J. Wiegold

Find a finite $p$-group that cannot be embedded in a finite $p$-group with trivial
multiplicator. Notice that every finite group can be embedded in a group with trivial
multiplicator.

The multiplicator (Schur multiplier) of a group $H$ is the second integral homology group
$M(H) = H_2(H, \mathbb{Z})$; for finite $H$ it is isomorphic to $H^2(H, \mathbb{C}^\times)$.
It is expressed here as `groupHomology.H2 (Rep.trivial ℤ H ℤ)`, the second homology of $H$
with coefficients in $\mathbb{Z}$ regarded as a trivial $H$-module. "Trivial multiplicator"
means that this group is a subsingleton.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«5.55»

/-- The trivial group has trivial multiplicator. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem subsingleton_H2_of_subsingleton (H : Type) [Group H] [Subsingleton H] :
    Subsingleton (groupHomology.H2 (Rep.trivial ℤ H ℤ)) :=
  ModuleCat.subsingleton_of_isZero <|
    isZero_groupHomology_succ_of_subsingleton (Rep.trivial ℤ H ℤ) 1

/--
Find a finite $p$-group that cannot be embedded in a finite $p$-group with trivial
multiplicator.

That is, do there exist a prime $p$ and a finite $p$-group $G$ such that no finite $p$-group
$H$ (for the same prime $p$) with trivial Schur multiplier $H_2(H, \mathbb{Z})$ contains a
subgroup isomorphic to $G$, i.e. such that there is no injective group homomorphism
$G \to H$ for any such $H$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«5.55» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (p : ℕ) (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (_ : Finite G), p.Prime ∧ IsPGroup p G ∧
      ∀ (H : Type) [Group H] [Finite H], IsPGroup p H →
        Subsingleton (groupHomology.H2 (Rep.trivial ℤ H ℤ)) →
        ¬ ∃ f : G →* H, Function.Injective f := by
  sorry

/--
Every finite group can be embedded in a group with trivial multiplicator.

The notebook does not say that the ambient group is finite, but the known result is that every
finite group $G$ embeds in a *finite* group $H$ with trivial Schur multiplier
$H_2(H, \mathbb{Z})$; this is the version stated here. The version with an arbitrary ambient
group is a consequence of it.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«5.55».variants.finite_group (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G] :
    ∃ (H : Type) (_ : Group H) (_ : Finite H),
      Subsingleton (groupHomology.H2 (Rep.trivial ℤ H ℤ)) ∧
        ∃ f : G →* H, Function.Injective f := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«5.55»

items: Schur multiplier ('multiplicator') is formalized as H_2(H, ℤ) = `groupHomology (Rep.trivial ℤ H ℤ) 2` (Mathlib group homology with ℤ as a trivial module); triviality is `Subsingleton` of the underlying type of this ModuleCat object. This is equivalent to `Limits.IsZero` (ModuleCat.isZero_iff_subsingleton); I verified in a scratch check that the trivial group satisfies the condition via `isZero_groupHomology_succ_of_subsingleton`. The alternative description H^2(H, ℂ^×) is equivalent for finite groups but not used.
'Embedded' is formalized as existence of an injective group homomorphism `G →* H`.

'p-group' is `IsPGroup p G` together with `Finite G`; the prime p is existentially quantified with `p.Prime` (needed since `IsPGroup` is degenerate for non-prime p) and is shared by G and the ambient group H, matching 'a finite p-group ... in a finite p-group'.
Groups live in `Type` (universe 0), as in the other Kourovka files; this is also forced by `Rep ℤ H` requiring H and ℤ in the same universe.
For the variant slot the ambient group H is required to be finite, following the decomposition table's note (the notebook text just says 'a group'); the docstring records this.

reviewer_notes: Composition: c01's two statements (edited to use `groupHomology.H2`, the Mathlib abbrev, and `¬ ∃ f, Function.Injective f`) plus c08's sanity test that the trivial group has trivial multiplier, stated inline without a bespoke definition (c07/c08's bespoke `schurMultiplier`/`HasTrivialSchurMultiplier` were unnecessary; a generic definition would belong in FormalConjecturesForMathlib anyway). Ambiguities: (1) 'multiplicator' = Schur multiplier, modelled as H₂(H,ℤ); for finite H this is isomorphic to H²(H,ℂ^×), so the choice is immaterial here since all groups involved are finite. (2) The prime p is implicitly existentially quantified and shared by G and the ambient H, following the table. (3) The 'Notice' sentence omits 'finite' for the ambient group; per the table the variant quantifies over finite H (the known result, e.g. G ≤ GL_n(q) ≤ SL_{n+1}(q) with SL_{n+1}(q) generically having trivial multiplier), and the docstring records this. No candidate omitted a slot; no objections to the decomposition were raised. File compiles with only `declaration uses 'sorry'` warnings.
